regions.name: Columbia River Gorge National Scenic Area
regions.scarcityHook: 1986 CRGNSA Act + SMA/GMA overlays + Goal 14 UGBs — six statutory layers stacked on 292,600 protected acres.
regions.regulatoryContext: The proving ground. The Columbia River Gorge National Scenic Area Act of 1986 created the country's first national-scenic-area land-use regime: a federally-appointed Commission reviewing development across 292,600 acres, layered over Oregon's Goal 14 urban growth boundaries on the south bank and Washington's Growth Management Act urban growth areas on the north bank. The result is the tightest land-supply collar in the Pacific Northwest — eleven micro-markets whose net buildable acreage, depletion horizons, and appreciation curves this platform quantifies.
regions.taxArbitrageNote: Oregon's progressive income tax (to 9.9%) vs Washington's zero personal income tax — cross-river commuting pairs (Dallesport↔The Dalles, White Salmon↔Hood River) quantify the spread.

regions.name: Puget Sound I-5 Corridor
regions.scarcityHook: The original UGB scarcity market: island cities, plateau enclaves, and mountain-walled UGAs pressed against the GMA's firmest lines in King and Kitsap counties.
regions.regulatoryContext: The Growth Management Act's flagship theater — six boundary-trapped micro-markets spanning a sole-source-aquifer island city (Bainbridge), a no-UGA rural island (Vashon), a floodplain-walled Ridge city (Snoqualmie), a fully-built plateau (Sammamish), an Issaquah-Apis-walled valley city, and a light-rail TOD inner ring (Shoreline). The corridor methodology ports directly: UGA residual land bands, per-jurisdiction depletion horizons, and the same net-vs-gross buildable ledger.
regions.taxArbitrageNote: WA 0% personal income tax vs CA's 13.3% top bracket — the equity-exodus arbitrage that prices King County land, captured at ferry-commute and I-90 distance from Seattle wages.

regions.name: Willamette Valley
regions.scarcityHook: Oregon Goal 14 at metro scale — Portland UGB reserves, Salem, Corvallis, Eugene inside the nation's oldest statewide growth boundary system.
regions.regulatoryContext: The Gorge's big sibling. Senate Bill 100 (1973) gave every Oregon city an urban growth boundary and rural lands exclusive-farm-use zoning. The Willamette Valley is where that system is stress-tested by metro demand: Portland's UGB reserve studies, Salem's expansion votes, and university-town scarcity in Corvallis and Eugene.
regions.taxArbitrageNote: OR zero sales tax ↔ WA zero income tax — the two-state shuffle, quantified per commuting pair.

regions.name: Vancouver ↔ Portland Border
regions.scarcityHook: The border arbitrage classic: Vancouver's UGA absorbing demand that Portland's UGB wall deflects north.
regions.regulatoryContext: Two growth-boundary systems meet at the Columbia's widest bridge gap. Vancouver WA's GMA urban growth area expands against Portland's fixed Goal 14 line — the cleanest natural experiment in North America for how boundary asymmetry prices land.
regions.taxArbitrageNote: Live in WA (0% income tax), shop in OR (0% sales tax) — the classic quantified.

regions.name: Bend / Redmond
regions.scarcityHook: UGB + state land + water rights — Central Oregon's tri-layer scarcity at the Cascades' foot.
regions.regulatoryContext: Bend's Goal 14 boundary against publicly-owned state and federal land, with groundwater mitigation requirements in the Deschutes basin adding a hydraulic constraint on top of the legal one. The fastest-appreciating Oregon market inside the tightest water-rights regime.
regions.taxArbitrageNote: CA equity exodus economics — the arbitrage is against California's top bracket, not a neighboring state.

regions.name: Hood Canal / Kitsap
regions.scarcityHook: GMA UGA squeeze + the Shoreline Management Act along the canal's shellfish-sensitive shorelines.
regions.regulatoryContext: Kitsap County's UGAs are hemmed by Puget Sound on three sides; shoreline designations, salmon-critical-areas ordinances, and naval reservation buffers make the buildable band measurably thin. A ferry-adjacent scarcity market with Seattle wages one boat ride away.
regions.taxArbitrageNote: Kitsap residency against Seattle wages — WA's 0% income tax captured at ferry-commute distance.

regions.name: Olympic Peninsula
regions.scarcityHook: GMA boundaries + water availability — Sequim and Port Angeles constrained by both ordinance and hydrology.
regions.regulatoryContext: The rain-shadow side of the Olympics: retiree inflow into Clallam and Jefferson county UGAs where municipal water firm yield, not zoning, is the binding constraint in half the buildable bands.
regions.taxArbitrageNote: Retiree inflow vs CA/OR pension taxation — WA taxes neither pensions nor income.

regions.name: Spokane ↔ Coeur d'Alene
regions.scarcityHook: GMA UGA on the Washington side vs Idaho county planning across the state line — boundary asymmetry at the Inland Empire scale.
regions.regulatoryContext: The new corridor pair: Spokane's growth-management urban growth areas press against Post Falls and Coeur d'Alene's looser county-review regimes. The same ledger method — net buildable bands per jurisdiction, depletion horizons, cross-border demand flows — that priced the Columbia Gorge applies directly.
regions.taxArbitrageNote: WA 0% income ↔ ID flat-rate income — the newest quantifiable border spread.

regions.name: Boulder County, CO
regions.scarcityHook: The hardest urban growth boundary in the US — a 75,000-acre service-area cap ringed by a sales-tax-funded open-space belt.
regions.regulatoryContext: Boulder's 1970s-era growth cap plus decades of open-space acquisition created the most acute boundary premium in the country. County-level transferable development rights and sub-county municipalities (Longmont, Lafayette, Louisville) give the ledger its micro-market structure.
regions.taxArbitrageNote: CO flat income tax — no border spread; the scarcity premium itself is the story.

regions.name: Lake Tahoe Basin
regions.scarcityHook: TRPA bi-state regional planning — scenic-threshold and coverage caps freeze development basin-wide.
regions.regulatoryContext: The Tahoe Regional Planning Agency governs both states under a compact with Congress: impervious-coverage allocations, scenic-quality thresholds, and a development-rights marketplace. The closest American analog to the CRGNSA's federal-state overlay.
regions.taxArbitrageNote: NV 0% income tax vs CA top bracket — the Incline Village residency shuffle, quantified.

regions.name: Lexington Bluegrass, KY
regions.scarcityHook: Rural Service Area boundary + the nation's oldest PDR farmland-preservation program.
regions.regulatoryContext: Fayette County's 1958 urban service boundary — the country's first — plus a purchase-of-development-rights program that has permanently protected the Inner Bluegrass horse farms. The scarcity story is agricultural, cultural, and statutory at once.
regions.taxArbitrageNote: KY flat income tax — the play is land, not tax.

regions.name: Montgomery County Ag Reserve, MD
regions.scarcityHook: A 93,000-acre Agricultural Reserve ring around DC, held by transferable development rights since 1980.
regions.regulatoryContext: The nation's most successful TDR program: downzoned farmland sells development rights into the county's down-county density receiving areas. The reserve forms a hard greenbelt around the nation's capital-region demand engine.
regions.taxArbitrageNote: MD progressive brackets + DC/VA cross-border commuting pairs.

regions.name: New Jersey Pinelands
regions.scarcityHook: A comprehensive management plan across a million-acre biosphere reserve — the East's CRGNSA analog.
regions.regulatoryContext: Federal legislation (1978) + an interstate compact + the Pinelands Comprehensive Management Plan govern a million acres of sandy pine barrens with strict growth-area allocation. The rural/seaside micro-market structure maps cleanly onto the corridor ledger method.
regions.taxArbitrageNote: NJ property-tax pressure vs PA just across the Delaware — a cost-of-carry arbitrage rather than income-tax.

regions.name: O'ahu, Hawai'i
regions.scarcityHook: State Land Use Urban District — island land exhaustion in its purest form.
regions.regulatoryContext: Hawai'i's State Land Use Commission classifies every acre into four districts; the Urban district on O'ahu is finite by geography. The depletion-ledger model is at its most literal here: when the urban land is built, it is done.
regions.taxArbitrageNote: High-bracket state income tax — scarcity is geographic, not fiscal.

regions.name: Metro Vancouver / Fraser Valley, BC
regions.scarcityHook: Agricultural Land Reserve + Urban Containment Boundary — the Gorge story at metro scale, in Canadian dollars.
regions.regulatoryContext: British Columbia's ALR (1973) fences the Fraser Valley's farmland while Metro Vancouver's regional growth strategy draws a hard urban containment boundary. The closest structural twin to the Columbia Gorge's statutory collar anywhere in North America.
regions.taxArbitrageNote: CAD pricing, BC PTT transfer tax + foreign-buyer band, no provincial capital-gains on a principal residence — a different carry calculus to model.

regions.name: GTA / Golden Horseshoe, ON
regions.scarcityHook: Greenbelt + Oak Ridges Moraine + Growth Plan density targets — the most litigated land collar in Canada.
regions.regulatoryContext: Ontario's 2005 Greenbelt Act and the Growth Plan for the Greater Golden Horseshoe bound the largest urban region in Canada. Provincial policy-plan layers (greenbelt, moraine, Niagara escarpment) create the micro-market banding the ledger method needs.
regions.taxArbitrageNote: Ontario LTT + NRST layers; CREA/MLS data licensing required before any listing feed.

regions.name: Montréal CMA, QC
regions.scarcityHook: CPTAQ agricultural-zone protection — Québec's provincial commission gates every non-farm use of zoned farmland.
regions.regulatoryContext: The Commission de protection du territoire agricole du Québec has held the metropolitan agricultural belt since 1978. Structural additions for this market: bilingual routing (Bill 96 requires a French edition), metric units, CAD formatting.
regions.taxArbitrageNote: Québec's marginal-bracket stack — with Bill 96 language compliance as the gating deliverable.

regions.name: Calgary–Edmonton Corridor, AB
regions.scarcityHook: No greenbelt — city-limit + land fragmentation, the control case that proves the model.
regions.regulatoryContext: Alberta's unbounded prairie cities grow by annexation, not boundary statute. Including a non-greenbelt region tests the platform's core claim: that the depletion-ledger signal is produced by regulation, not by geography alone.
regions.taxArbitrageNote: AB property transfer fee only; no land-registry friction — the frictionless baseline.

submarkets.name: Cascade Locks
submarkets.waterPurveyor: City of Cascade Locks (well field; firm-yield concerns)
submarkets.primaryConstraints: Groundwater supply margin; Herman Creek floodplain; tribal fishing-site adjacency; WUI fire risk Class 4.
submarkets.summaryNarrative: The west-Gorge value market on the Oregon side: 110–135 net buildable acres, a real downtown marine grid, and the lowest Oregon-side baseline after the UGB walls of Hood River push demand east. Water-system firm yield is the variable to watch.

submarkets.name: Hood River
submarkets.waterPurveyor: City of Hood River Water Dept. (Buck Creek watershed + wells)
submarkets.wastewaterSystem: City of Hood River WWTP (river outfall, near capacity)
submarkets.primaryConstraints: GMA/SMA scenic overlay; steep-slope hazard zones on the west heights; effectively flat developable land nearly exhausted; WUI fire risk Class 4.
submarkets.summaryNarrative: The corridor's appreciation leader. Wind-sport tourism, orchard heritage and Portland-metro spillover demand collide with a nearly built-out Goal 14 UGB. Inventory turnover is the fastest in the Gorge; new product is overwhelmingly infill and redevelopment.

submarkets.name: Mosier
submarkets.waterPurveyor: City of Mosier (two-well field; seasonal nitrate pressure)
submarkets.primaryConstraints: Smallest UGB in the corridor; well capacity and nitrate margins; I-84 noise shed; WUI fire risk Class 5.
submarkets.summaryNarrative: The corridor's scarcity singularity: 15–25 net acres inside a 180-acre UGB. Mosier prices like a boutique market because it is one — every listing is effectively the last listing. First projected to reach terminal raw-land depletion (2032).

submarkets.name: The Dalles
submarkets.waterPurveyor: City of The Dalles (South Fork Mill Creek watershed + auxiliary wells)
submarkets.wastewaterSystem: City of The Dalles WWTP (mid-river outfall)
submarkets.primaryConstraints: UGB largely committed; data-center and light-industrial demand competes for residential land; WUI fire risk Class 4 on south hills.
submarkets.summaryNarrative: The largest land bank in the corridor, anchored by data-center payrolls and port industrial employment. Residential absorption is steady rather than spectacular, but the scale of net buildable acreage gives The Dalles the longest raw-land runway east of Bonneville.

submarkets.name: Bainbridge Island
submarkets.waterPurveyor: City of Bainbridge Island Utilities (sole-source island aquifer, 7 production wells)
submarkets.wastewaterSystem: Winslow WWTP (capacity-limited) + widespread on-site septic outside Winslow
submarkets.primaryConstraints: Sole-source island aquifer with declining static levels; salmon-bearing stream CAOs; SMA shoreline designations on 75% of perimeter; 35-min ferry capacity ceiling; tree canopy retention code.
submarkets.summaryNarrative: A 35-minute ferry from Seattle's core, entirely incorporated since 1991 — the island IS the city, and its UGA can never expand. King-County-caliber wages meet a fixed 90–120-acre net-buildable band over a sole-source aquifer. Every new lot is an infill or subdivision remnant; waterfront and view parcels clear $2M+ as a matter of course.

submarkets.name: Bingen
submarkets.primaryConstraints: Industrial buffer around the port; BNSF rail adjacency; partial-planning review; WUI fire risk Class 4.
submarkets.summaryNarrative: White Salmon's working-class twin across the flat: shared sewer capacity, port employment, and 35–50 net acres priced 35% below its neighbor. The value case is infrastructure parity with a lower land basis.

submarkets.name: Dallesport
submarkets.wastewaterSystem: Port of Klickitat / Dallesport lagoon WWTP (capacity headroom)
submarkets.primaryConstraints: Partial-planning jurisdiction (county-level review); rail and barge freight corridors bisect the UGA; WUI fire risk Class 5; SMA shoreline overlay along the Columbia.
submarkets.summaryNarrative: The purest cross-river tax-arbitrage play in the Gorge: zero Washington personal income tax, a bridge commute to The Dalles job base, and 140–180 acres of genuinely flat, infrastructure-served net buildable land. The 2036–2040 buildout window makes Dallesport the corridor's most credible appreciation compounder.

submarkets.name: Issaquah
submarkets.waterPurveyor: Cascade Water Alliance (Tolt supply, Issaquah zone)
submarkets.wastewaterSystem: King County Regional system (Issaquah interceptor; Sammamish Valley plant capacity headroom)
submarkets.primaryConstraints: Issaquah Alps (Cougar, Tiger, Squak mountains) wall the UGA on three sides; legacy coal-mine hazard areas; landslide hazard zones on the benches; I-90 is the only access spine; Highlands PUD in final phases.
submarkets.summaryNarrative: The mountain-walled valley city: growth can only go vertical in the Central Issaquah Plan footprint or uphill into the last Highlands phases. Legacy coal-mine hazard areas sterilize chunks of the remaining band, and the Issaquah Alps conservation walls make every expansion vote a constitutional event. 150–185 net acres is the honest residue.

submarkets.name: Lyle
submarkets.wastewaterSystem: Community septic; clustered treatment proposed but unfunded
submarkets.primaryConstraints: Septic-limited buildout; Klickitat River flood fringe; partial-planning review; WUI fire risk Class 5; rail corridor adjacency.
submarkets.summaryNarrative: A small UGA whose 5.4% projected CAGR outruns its infrastructure: appreciation is driven by scarcity (55–70 net acres), Klickitat River recreation access and White Salmon spillover — not by utility capacity. Buyers are underwriting land, not entitlement velocity.

submarkets.name: North Bonneville
submarkets.primaryConstraints: Hamilton Creek floodplain; deed-restricted platted lots from the 1930s relocation grid; WUI fire risk Class 4.
submarkets.summaryNarrative: A planned town born of the Bonneville Dam relocation, with municipal sewer and water already in the ground. Only 30–40 net acres remain; the story here is small-lot efficiency and zero-income-tax residency within minutes of Cascade Locks employment.

submarkets.name: Sammamish
submarkets.waterPurveyor: Cascade Water Alliance (Tolt + Tacoma supply blends)
submarkets.wastewaterSystem: King County Regional system (Sammamish Plateau divider to South Plant)
submarkets.primaryConstraints: Plateau fully platted — no greenfield land remains; Lake Sammamish phosphorus TMDL caps impervious runoff; 35% tree-canopy code; East Lake Sammamish landslide benches; town-center up-zone is the only density valve.
submarkets.summaryNarrative: The region's highest baseline and earliest depletion: a fully-platted plateau city whose only growth valve is a contested town center. Lake Sammamish water-quality rules cap impervious surface while $1.65M medians bid up teardown and lot-split remnants. Supply here is arithmetic — the platted grid is complete.

submarkets.name: Shoreline
submarkets.waterPurveyor: Seattle Public Utilities via wholesale + Alderwood Water District edges
submarkets.wastewaterSystem: King County Regional system (Ronald transfer; West Point plant)
submarkets.primaryConstraints: 185th St Link station-area construction windows gate the up-zone; Boeing Creek and riparian corridors cut the grid; single-family character overlays slow parcel consolidation; Aurora (SR-99) corridor noise + OSHA setbacks.
submarkets.summaryNarrative: The TOD conversion play: an inner-ring Seattle suburb re-platting around a light-rail station that opened in 2024. The 110–140-acre net band is consolidation remnants between single-family character overlays — assembly risk, not land supply, is the binding constraint. The 4.9% CAGR is the region's most infrastructure-leveraged.

submarkets.name: Snoqualmie
submarkets.waterPurveyor: City of Snoqualmie (Tolt River supply via Cascade Water Alliance)
submarkets.wastewaterSystem: City of Snoqualmie WWTP (Snoqualmie River outfall)
submarkets.primaryConstraints: Snoqualmie River 100-yr floodplain constrains the valley floor; salmon-critical FW-zone buffers; Mount Si NRCA and conservation lands wall the east; Snoqualmie Ridge PUD is in terminal buildout phases.
submarkets.summaryNarrative: A city boxed by geography: the river's floodplain below, Mount Si's conservation wall above, and the Snoqualmie Ridge master-planned community entering its final phases. The 5.4% CAGR is what happens when Eastside and Seattle tech demand funnels down the I-90 corridor into the last flat, infrastructure-served land before the Cascades.

submarkets.name: Stevenson
submarkets.waterPurveyor: City of Stevenson (Rock Creek surface + wells)
submarkets.primaryConstraints: Steep terrain and landslide hazard zones; Rock Creek floodplain; partial-planning county overlay; WUI fire risk Class 4.
submarkets.summaryNarrative: The west-Gorge lifestyle anchor: full municipal utilities, a genuine walkable main street, and Portland-weekend demand. Buildable land is constrained by slope more than by ordinance, which keeps 90–110 net acres trickling onto the market slowly and prices compounding near 5.1%.

submarkets.name: Vashon Island
submarkets.waterPurveyor: Private wells only (Vashon-Maury sole-source aquifer, Stage 1 GWMA advisory)
submarkets.wastewaterSystem: On-site septic only — no municipal sewer on the island
submarkets.primaryConstraints: No UGA exists — rural densities locked by the King County Comprehensive Plan (1 dwelling / 10–20 ac typical); sole-source aquifer; septic-only buildout; ferry-dependent (Fauntleroy + Southworth); forest retention standards.
submarkets.summaryNarrative: The terminal scarcity case: a King County island with NO urban growth area, where the GMA's rural designation caps new lots at one per 10–20 acres and both water and sewer are private. The 40–55-acre net band is lot-split remnants — supply can literally never respond to Seattle demand, which is the whole thesis of this platform compressed into one land market.

submarkets.name: White Salmon
submarkets.waterPurveyor: City of White Salmon (Buck Creek + spring sources)
submarkets.primaryConstraints: Buildable bench nearly exhausted; steep slopes above and below town; view premiums inflate land basis; WUI fire risk Class 4.
submarkets.summaryNarrative: The second-fastest compounder in the corridor and the only full-planning GMA city in Klickitat County. White Salmon pairs Hood River views without Oregon income tax — a structural demand magnet. Net buildable land is the binding constraint: 45–60 acres against 5.6% projected CAGR.

submarkets.name: Wishram
submarkets.primaryConstraints: BNSF mainline adjacency; zero municipal sewer; remoteness from employment centers; WUI fire risk Class 5.
submarkets.summaryNarrative: The corridor's entry-price market. Wishram trades at the lowest baseline in the Gorge on the strength of river access and rail-town character; with no sewer and only 25–35 net acres, its ceiling is a lifestyle market rather than a growth market.

listings.title: GMA Luxury Farm & Vineyard Estate with High-Value Residence
listings.description: Flagship corridor asset: 38.5 deed acres under GMA Agriculture with certified water rights and south-facing Mt. Hood and Columbia views. The 5,800 sq ft custom residence is sited for visual subordinance under CRGNSA review — non-reflective finishes, earth-tone palette, and a low-profile roofline screened by retained oak grove. Established vineyard blocks (11 acres), climate-controlled farm shop, and a fully entitled second homesite make this the benchmark agricultural compound in the National Scenic Area.

listings.title: Waterline Contemporary on the Island's South End
listings.description: Cedar-and-blackened-steel contemporary set low against a westward water view — the compliance posture that island review rewards. Moored three miles from the ferry, inside a 90–120-acre net-buildable band that can never grow. Agate Pass frontage, rainshadow garden, and a permitted studio above the garage make this the benchmark island asset.

listings.title: Plateau Lakefront with Private Dock
listings.description: 115 feet of Lake Sammamish frontage with a permitted dock — in a city whose platted grid is finished and whose 2034 depletion horizon is the region's earliest. Lakefront is the fixed supply of last resort; the phosphorus TMDL makes every rebuild a review event. Hold, lease, and let arithmetic work.

listings.title: Central Issaquah Vertical Mixed-Use Parcel
listings.description: 0.62 acres in the Central Issaquah Plan's core — the only place in the city where height and density are by right. Six stories as-of-right, transit-spine frontage. The value is the entitlement, not the dirt: mountain walls on three sides make the CIP the terminal growth valve.

listings.title: Cougar Mountain View Estate
listings.description: Terraced decks above the Issaquah valley floor with Seattle and Lake Sammamish in the sightline. Coal-mine hazard review cleared; landslide benches engineered. Inside the mountain-walled city's 150–185-acre residue — the last view land before the Issaquah Alps conservation wall.

listings.title: Island Farmstead on 10 Deed Acres
listings.description: Classic Vashon hold: farmhouse, restored barn, and fenced pasture under RA-10 — the rural designation that caps density at one dwelling per ten acres. Well and septic, ferry-dependent, and forever outside any urban growth area. This is scarcity-an-al-purpose land: it cannot be subdivided into existence.

listings.title: Orchard District Farmhouse on Irrigated Acreage
listings.description: Historic farmhouse surrounded by producing pear and cherry blocks with district irrigation water rights. Classic Hood River agricultural land-bank play: hold the orchard income while the UGB infill premium migrates outward.

listings.title: 185th Station TOD Townhome Row
listings.description: Assembled row of four 1950s parcels one block from the 185th Street Link station — the TOD up-zone the city spent a decade approving. Eight townhomes by right in the TC-4 envelope. Assembly-complete, character-overlay cleared, light rail in service: the region's cleanest infrastructure-arbitrage underwrite.

listings.title: Cliffside View Home Above the River
listings.description: Cantilevered residence on the basalt bench with a 180-degree Columbia Gorge view corridor. Inside the corridor's second-fastest compounder (5.6% CAGR) and its most land-constrained full-planning city — 45–60 net acres remain.

listings.title: Ridge Craftsman Steps from the Falls Trail
listings.description: Late-phase Snoqualmie Ridge craftsman with Mount Si framing the street. The PUD that added 2,200 homes is entering terminal phases — 120–150 net acres region-wide, floodplain-walled below and conservation-walled above. I-90 tech commute, falls trailhead at the end of the block.

listings.title: Heights Infill Craftsman — New Construction
listings.description: One of the last buildable interior lots on the Heights. New-construction craftsman with ADI-ready utility stubs, two blocks to schools and the Heights business district. Walk-score positioning inside a nearly exhausted Goal 14 UGB.

listings.title: Downtown Mixed-Use Redevelopment Parcel
listings.description: Assemblage opportunity across two street-front lots in the certified historic downtown. Zoned C-2 with vertical mixed-use by right — the corridor's cleanest workforce-housing underwrite with port and data-center payroll demand within two miles.

listings.title: Baker Creek City-View Contemporary
listings.description: Terraced hillside contemporary above Baker Creek with protected river-view corridor. Positioned inside The Dalles' slowest-appreciating but deepest land bank — 175–205 net acres of remaining UGB capacity backs long-hold value.

listings.title: Klickitat River Acreage with Water Right
listings.description: 12.6 acres at the Klickitat confluence with a senior irrigation right and SMA-review building envelope. Inside Lyle's 55–70-acre net-buildable band — the highest CAGR per acre of infrastructure in the corridor, if septic capacity holds.

listings.title: Banked View Lot Above Tramp Harbor
listings.description: 2.4 wooded acres with a permitted-view building envelope — pending lot-of-record confirmation, the only path to a new Vashon homesite. Well site approved; septic design banked. Inside a market where 40–55 net acres IS the entire remaining supply.

listings.title: Pocket-UGB Cottage Remodel
listings.description: A rare turnover inside the smallest UGB in the Gorge — 15–25 net acres total. The 2032 depletion projection makes every Mosier listing a terminal-supply asset; remodel already completed to systems level.

listings.title: New Construction w/ WA Tax Arbitrage
listings.description: Builder-spec residence completed inside the UGA's 140–180-acre buildable reserve. Priced $60k under the Oregon-side median while its owner keeps 100% of personal income — the purest illustration of the cross-river spread.

listings.title: Rock Creek Cottage — Walk-In Condition
listings.description: Remodeled cottage two blocks from Stevenson's Rock Creek main street. Full municipal utilities inside the west Gorge's only full-service lifestyle city with 90–110 net acres of remaining buildable supply.

listings.title: Jewett Infill Duplex Development Site
listings.description: Shovel-ready R-3 site with joint WWTP allocation from the White Salmon/Bingen plant. Duplex-by-right entitlement within walking distance of the full-planning city's commercial core.

listings.title: Port-Adjacent Light Industrial Flex Site
listings.description: Graded 1.1-acre GI site with rail-served adjacency and joint WWTP allocation. The value pairing to White Salmon: identical infrastructure, 35% lower land basis, 35–50 net acres remaining.

listings.title: Columbia Riverfront Cabin Retreat
listings.description: Water-proximate cabin on the corridor's lowest rung of the price ladder. Septic-only, rail-adjacent, and remote — but the 4.3% projected CAGR still compounds from a $305k baseline.

listings.title: UGA Ready-to-Build Bluff View Parcel
listings.description: Flat, cleared 1.4-acre parcel inside the Dallesport UGA with PUD water and Port sewer at the property line. Direct river view across to The Dalles. The textbook zero-income-tax arbitrage entry: build in Washington, commute four minutes to Oregon employment.

listings.title: Marina District Buildable Lot
listings.description: Half-acre lot steps from the marina grid inside a 110–135-acre net-buildable UGB. City water and sewer connected; well-documented firm-yield margin is the only diligence item.

listings.title: Hamilton Creek Infill Lot
listings.description: Buildable lot on the historic relocation grid with Skamania PUD water and city sewer at the line. Entry ticket to zero-income-tax Washington inside a 30–40-acre net-buildable envelope.
